newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clear starts paying tax, ups operating profit.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clear starts paying tax, ups operating profit.

text.p: Clear Communications' net profit fall to NZ$23.4 million in the March year from $29 million a year earlier reflected the fact that Clear started paying tax in the 1995-6 year, Chief Executive Andrew Makin said on Friday.
The tax bill came to NZ$13.84 million.
On an operating level, Clear reported a pre-tax profit of NZ$37.27 million, a sharp improvement from $29.0 million.
Dividends paid during the year totalled NZ$12 million.
Total retained earnings were NZ$1.28 million from an accumulated loss of $10.15 million the previous year.
Initial start-up losses had been offset against previous year's taxable income, with Clear becoming a full tax payer in 1996, Makin told Reuters.
Clear operates in competition with Telecom Corp of New Zealand Ltd in the long distance telephone market.
"Market share seems to have stabilised at around 20 percent," Makin said.

While Clear, like other network operators Telecom and BellSouth, were enjoying increased volume, there had also been intense pressure on margins as new competitors clambered into the the New Zealand market.

Clear was continuing to roll out new services which had contributed to the increase in revenues and profitability over the March year. Clear's Internet service, Clearnet, had been "phenomenally successful," Makin said.

Makin said the question of number portability looked no closer to being resolved, but he noted caretaker Communications Minister Maurice Williamson had commented before the election that he was watching the situation closely.

In a statement accompanying the result, Clear Chairman John Ede said: "There is still virtually no choice for consumers in local calling and little will change until key issues like number portability have been resolved."
Clear is owned in equal proportions by British Telecom, MCI Communications Corp, the New Zealand family-owned Todd Corp and state-owned Television New Zealand. -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
